seed_notes: Initial Buyer Voice vendor-score dataset. Scores evaluate the readiness of each vendor-specific GEAR corpus and report package for Buyer Voice analysis, not product capability or market performance.

vendors.specialization: Buyer Voice corpus: OpenAI interactions and market cuts
vendors.description: OpenAI Buyer Voice package built from a large 2026 YTD GEAR interaction corpus. The package supports full-corpus discovery plus market-cut reports for enterprise AI assistants and enterprise AI coding agents.
vendors.capability_analysis: Strong source-corpus and interaction-spine readiness because the raw GEAR export, formatted corpus workflow, and sample corpus metadata are defined. The report model is ready for standard rail presentation, but validation remains a readiness gap until evidence-ledger, redaction, and claim-check automation are implemented.
vendors.key_differentiators: Large interaction volume; multiple market-cut report paths; strong fit for unconstrained theme discovery and buyer-language theme synthesis.

sub_pillar_rationale.SRC-01: Raw and derived package artifacts are inventoried in the schema and report model.
sub_pillar_rationale.SRC-02: Corpus metadata includes anchor, date range, quarters, and record count.
sub_pillar_rationale.SRC-03: Formatter script and formatted text workflow are identified, but checksum automation is not yet wired.
sub_pillar_rationale.INT-01: GEAR reference, question, summary, date, purpose, and raw fields are preserved by the schema.
sub_pillar_rationale.INT-02: Buyer profile mapping covers role, region, sector, market, persona, and enterprise size.
sub_pillar_rationale.INT-03: Vendor and analyst context are mapped; ambiguous mentions still need extraction/QA logic.
sub_pillar_rationale.RUN-01: Report tabs and prompt-informed runs are modeled; run registry automation remains pending.
sub_pillar_rationale.RUN-02: Market-cut and qualifying set concepts exist, but exact qualifying-reference lists need generation.
sub_pillar_rationale.RUN-03: Full corpus and market-cut modes are represented with discovery-first guidance.
sub_pillar_rationale.THM-01: Designed for buyer-language theme discovery from the full corpus.
sub_pillar_rationale.THM-02: Category assignment is supported after discovery, though OpenAI reports are primarily market-cut driven.
sub_pillar_rationale.RAT-01: Spread rating guidance exists; calibrated thresholds remain intentionally qualitative.
sub_pillar_rationale.RAT-02: Trajectory gates are defined, but period-window support needs generated evidence tables.
sub_pillar_rationale.RAT-03: Optional sentiment and competitive framing are modeled without forcing taxonomy.
sub_pillar_rationale.EVD-01: Reference and excerpt requirements are explicit; evidence ledger extraction remains pending.
sub_pillar_rationale.EVD-02: Buyer versus analyst attribution is a first-class rule.
sub_pillar_rationale.EVD-03: Sensitivity and redaction policy is documented; automated blocker detection remains pending.
sub_pillar_rationale.OUT-01: Claim registry model supports report output and validation status.
sub_pillar_rationale.OUT-02: Slide suppression rules for counts and references are explicit.
sub_pillar_rationale.VAL-01: Reference/rating QA checks are defined but not yet automated end to end.
sub_pillar_rationale.VAL-02: Figure and buyer-composition QA checks are defined but need generated support artifacts.
sub_pillar_rationale.VAL-03: Attribution and redaction QA rules are clear; automation is the remaining gap.

vendors.specialization: Buyer Voice corpus: ServiceNow commercial friction categories
vendors.source_file: buyervoice/Corpora - Raw GEAR/GEAR - ServiceNow Commercial Friction Set.csv
vendors.description: ServiceNow Buyer Voice package built from a large 2026 YTD GEAR interaction corpus focused on commercial friction. The package supports supplied-category analysis, theme synthesis, deep dives, and executive-style briefing outputs.
vendors.capability_analysis: Very strong source and scope readiness because the corpus is large, category-directed, and aligned to a commercial-friction briefing use case. It is slightly stronger than the OpenAI package on supplied-category/report-shape readiness, while sharing the same validation automation gap around evidence ledgering, redaction, and claim support.
vendors.key_differentiators: Large corpus; client-supplied commercial-friction categories; strong fit for tabbed deep-dive reports and executive briefing slides.
